answer_1.quote: The primary objective is to train a reward model capable of training a policy that generates high-quality texts, as evaluated by humans, using a constrained set of human-annotated data.
answer_1.outputs: The outputs consist of 2 components: • Predictive scores s (x i ,y + i ) and s (x i ,y - i ) for each example (x i , y + i , y - i ), indicating the model's assessment of the relative quality of the summaries; • The reward model f ϕ : X × Y → E, where E is the embedding space.

answer_2.quote: Our scoring criteria encompass factual accuracy, text relevance, information completeness, and clarity of expression, are uniformly applied. Each dimension receives a score up to 10, with increments of 0.5. The overall score is derived from the average of four metrics.

answer_3.quote: To ensure the consistency and integrity of the evaluation, we employ  to assess all outputs from GPT-J (6B) ) across four dimensions. This methodology aligns with various studies highlighting the capabilities of LLMs to produce high-quality text evaluation that align with or surpass human judgments.

answer_4.quote: Initially, human annotators assess model outputs and provide feedback. This feedback is then utilized in the reward modeling process, where supervised learning is used to train a reward model that replicates human assessments.
answer_4.guideline: The primary objective is to train a reward model capable of training a policy that generates high-quality texts, as evaluated by humans, using a constrained set of human-annotated data.
